question: Why might one attain a state beyond pleasure and pain or of the nature of bliss?
premises: One may attain a form devoid of pleasure and pain.
One may alternatively attain a form of the nature of bliss.
The attained state corresponds to what is remembered in consciousness.
inference: Even higher or neutral states at separation are determined by what consciousness remembers.
plain_english: Or if one attains a state devoid of pleasure and pain, or one of the nature of bliss, why does one go to that? Because that is what this one remembers in consciousness.
